transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I don’t get any enjoyment out of the things I used to love doing, and I can’t make myself start anything anymore. I used to spend hours on my model railways or woodworking, but now I just sit there and can't bring myself to even touch them.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable, lasting for several days, which was very different from your usual self?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I've never had periods of abnormally high energy or felt unusually high or irritable. It has really been the exact opposite for me.
Have you felt this low and unmotivated for at least two years, or are these symptoms occurring in distinct episodes separated by periods where you felt like your normal self?

No, it hasn't been nearly that long. This heavy, joyless feeling really started about a month ago after a promising work contract fell through. Before this past month, I still felt pretty much like my normal self.
Since this started a month ago, have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, appetite, or your ability to focus on daily tasks?

Yes, all three have been heavily affected; I can't fall asleep until 2 or 3 AM because my mind loops with worries, and I often forget to eat until late afternoon because I have no appetite. My brain also feels like molasses, making it incredibly hard to focus on simple emails or make basic decisions like paying bills.
Since these symptoms began a month ago, have you been able to continue working or managing your basic daily responsibilities, or have these symptoms made it nearly impossible to function?

It has been incredibly hard to function lately. I’ve completely stopped looking for new consulting leads and even missed a few bill payments because I couldn't face the paperwork. I’ve also been canceling on my friends and book club because any kind of social interaction just feels like too much to handle.
Would you describe your current state as having a complete, profound loss of pleasure in almost all activities and a total lack of reactivity to any positive news or events?

Yes, that is exactly what it feels like. It’s as if all the enjoyment has been switched off in my brain, and even if something positive happens, I feel no spark or reaction at all. I can't even bring myself to touch my woodworking or go for a bike ride because nothing feels worth the effort anymore.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a profound loss of interest and pleasure (anhedonia) in all activities, accompanied by significant somatic symptoms (insomnia, loss of appetite, cognitive slowing) and severe functional impairment. The symptoms are acute (1 month duration) and characterized by a total lack of reactivity, consistent with a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms.
